# Troubleshooting

## When to use this guide

A `corelink-go` call is returning an unexpected error or stalling. Use the
table below to map errors to the canonical fix in
`docs/reference/error-taxonomy`.

## Diagnostic flow

```go
rep, err := cli.Doctor(ctx)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
for _, c := range rep.Checks {
    log.Printf("%s %s %s", c.Name, c.Status, c.NextActionDoc)
}
```

Same 8 checks as `corelink doctor --json`: network, auth, storage-write,
storage-read, BYOK, region, quota, client-verify.

## Common errors

| Error code | Type | First action |
|---|---|---|
| `COR_AUTH_001` | `*AuthError` | Re-export `CORELINK_PAT`; check scopes via `cli.Whoami(ctx)` |
| `COR_AUTH_002` | `*AuthError` | PAT revoked; mint a new one |
| `COR_QUOTA_001` | `*QuotaError` | Tenant over storage cap |
| `COR_REGION_001` | `*RegionError` | Use regional endpoint; `corelink stat` reveals home region |
| `COR_VERIFY_001` | `*DigestMismatchError` | Discard bytes; retry; persistent → Sev-2 |
| `COR_NET_001` | `*ConnectError` | `corelink doctor network` — egress filtering likely |

## Goroutine leaks

The most common Go-specific failure mode is dropping a streaming reader
without `Close()`:

```go
// WRONG — leaks a connection and the verify goroutine
rc, _ := cli.GetStream(ctx, digest)
io.ReadAll(rc)

// RIGHT
rc, err := cli.GetStream(ctx, digest)
if err != nil { ... }
defer rc.Close()
```

`Close()` returns an error when the BLAKE3 root fails to verify — check it.

## Verbose logging

```bash
export CORELINK_LOG=debug
```

The SDK writes structured JSON to `stderr`. Pipe through `jq`:

```bash
./build 2>&1 | jq 'select(.level=="error")'
```

## Filing a bug

Include `corelink doctor --json` and `cli.Whoami(ctx)` output. Never include
your PAT.
